segmentation.text: the driver of the vehicle on the left
to the vehicle on the right.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: 'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'): the subject and the other vehicle v both.

Two vehicles 'enter' at approximately the same time when they reach its entrance together: a vehicle that yields at the edge never enters together with the other, so the entering the words time is each vehicle's arrival at X — occupying a carrier entering X (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), its body comes within the stop-point tolerance of X, the bound within which a vehicle is at a mark (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)'). Not a stand-in for occupancy: the distance reads arrival at the edge, the carrier fixes which intersection.

'From different highways' (DEF-NRS-484A-095): the two approach carriers c1, c2 (st.lane_enters) lie on ways (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') such that c2 lies on a highway on which c1 does not lie.
The subject is the vehicle on the left: the other vehicle lies on its right, rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of" ...)'. 'Driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.
Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while v is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).
'The vehicle on the right': v of the admitted aggregate whose bearing in the subject's frame (rel.bearing) has a negative lateral component (to the right) at the later of the two arrivals.

Same mapping as 'or at a traffic-controlled intersection' in the index: a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering X (dev.governs; DEF-NRS-484A-145 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic').

Per rel.oncoming's not-a-stand-in clause, the direction a road user approaches from is read through its approach carrier and that carrier's st.lane_direction: c1 and c2 have designated directions opposed within p.oncoming_heading_cos.

'Is making a left turn': the vehicle's heading change since its entry into X (rel.occupies), integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('positive when the heading turns to the left'), lies to the left between p.turn_heading_min and p.u_turn_heading_min.

operationalizations.standard: approximately the same time: the two arrivals at the intersection's edge are close enough in time that neither vehicle can clear before the other arrives
operationalizations.convention: arrival of each vehicle is the observation (kin.time) at which its body first comes within p.stop_point_tolerance of X on a carrier entering X; the two arrivals are at approximately the same time where their times differ by no more than p.same_time_arrival_window, a two-second headway

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

applicability: At every observation at which the subject has arrived at an intersection X — its arrival: the latest observation at which, occupying a carrier c1 with st.lane_enters(c1, X), its body came within p.stop_point_tolerance of X (st.region_geometry distance) having not been within it at the observation before — and has occupied c1 or X at every observation since; except where X is controlled (a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering X), and except where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 or NRS_484B_250_4_o2 (binder subject ↦ subject) applies to the subject.
obligation: Re-binding c1 and X as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that arrived at X in the same way on a carrier c2 entering X, c2 lying on a highway (st.on_way) on which c1 does not lie, with the two arrivals no more than p.same_time_arrival_window apart (time since each arrival), v lying on the subject's right at the later of the two arrivals (rel.bearing lateral component negative), and v occupying c2 or X at every observation since its arrival — excepting the pair where c1's and c2's designated directions have a dot product below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos and the subject or v declares int.left_turn at X at this observation or v's heading change since its latest entry into X (heading-since over kin.yaw_rate, step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is a left turn of at least p.turn_heading_min and below p.u_turn_heading_min: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'official' is a legal status; the device present and governing is its evidence.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled X. The subject on c1 and v on c2 (on another highway) arrive within p.same_time_arrival_window of each other; v lies to the subject's right (rel.bearing). The subject proceeds with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same arrivals; the subject comes to rest at X's edge until v has crossed, then proceeds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A dev.yield_sign governs c1: X is controlled.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled X; simultaneous arrivals from different highways with v on the subject's right; the subject and v are not in contact and their centres' closest approach lies within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance; kin.speed is not observed, so whether the subject proceeds rather than holding at rest is unknown. (rel.bearing is computed from positions and headings and is not a mask that can blank which vehicle is on the right.)

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Simultaneous arrivals; v lies to the subject's left; the subject proceeds first in conflict with v: no vehicle on its right is owed the right-of-way.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: v on the subject's right arrives several times p.same_time_arrival_window after the subject; the subject proceeds: not approximately the same time.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject arrives at uncontrolled X with no other road user in the scene.
